problem: When institutional events are concurrent or their order is not yet established, is there a unique actionable Now, a visible set of competing bindings, or latent transition ambiguity hidden behind one current projection?
methodologicalAnalogy: Jepsen-style history generation/fault pressure plus an independent enumerating checker. The apparatus does not assume one arrival order is authoritative: every permutation consistent with the frozen concurrent batch is an admissible sequentialization.

historyModel.base: A sequential prefix with known order.
historyModel.concurrentBatch: 2-3 events with no order relation inside the batch.
historyModel.admissibleExecutions: All unique permutations of the concurrent batch appended to the base.
historyModel.bindingSet: Unique Orthogonal Frontier cores produced by admissible executions.
historyModel.continuationSet: Unique owner-side ContinuationKernel v0 states produced by admissible executions.

classifications.DETERMINATE: one binding core and one continuation kernel
classifications.LATENT_CONTINUATION_AMBIGUITY: one binding core but more than one continuation kernel

targetedRaces: two concurrent lawful elections for different office-holders
root compromise concurrent with in-band root rotation
lawful succession concurrent with predecessor sanction
single authority claim concurrent with clear_claims
external refoundation concurrent with root compromise
valid amendment concurrent with physical tamper
safeConsequenceRule: Fresh consequential institutional action is ALLOW only if every admissible execution yields consequentialAuthorityStatus=AUTHORIZED with the same office-holder and effective controller. Otherwise the conservative result is HOLD.
guards: The checker reports a set of admissible results; it must never choose a preferred linearization without evidence.
LATENT_CONTINUATION_AMBIGUITY is not exposed as current binding disagreement, but it blocks claiming the projection is transition-determinate.
A sequentialization-dependent result is not automatically a bug in the institution; it may indicate missing ordering/coordination/decision procedure.
This stage is deterministic substrate research. Agent behavior is deferred until representative ambiguity classes are frozen.
